newsitem.title: USA: Blue Cross of NJ, Anthem to let merger pact expire.
newsitem.headline: Blue Cross of NJ, Anthem to let merger pact expire.

text.p: Blue Cross and Blue Shield of New Jersey and Anthem Inc said Tuesday they have agreed to let their merger pact expire June 30.
In a joint release, the companies said regulatory obstacles and litigation over their proposed merger make it unlikely that they will close the deal before the deadline expires.
As such, the companies said "little or no purpose in extending the current merger agreement."
The two insurance companies initiated merger proceedings in 1995, they said. Their combination would have created a $9 billion-a-year health care management company.

While both boards of directors approved the deal, Blue Cross has been unable to complete the necessary conversion to a mutual insurance company because of regulatory issues and litigation, it said. Anthem is already a mutual company.
Blue Cross said it would continue its efforts to convert to mutual status.

Anthem said it will continue with its plans to develop an East Coast regional operation known as Anthem East. It will also continue with plans to merge with Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Connecticut, it said.
